summary: Build a fullscreen 200x200 grid-based (Game of Life-like) animation with black grid lines, white cells, two states (live=black, dead=white), 50 randomly placed live cells in the center at start, reset regenerating 3000 randomly placed live cells in the center, start/pause/reset controls, zoom in/out, generation updates every 0.5s using standard Life birth/survival/death rules, and add speed up/down controls that double/halve the update interval.
architectural_notes: UI requires start/pause/reset controls and zoomable viewport.
2D cellular automaton (Game of Life-like) simulation on a 200x200 grid with a fixed 0.5s tick rate.
Start state spawns 50 live cells randomly within a central region; reset spawns 3000 live cells randomly within the central region.
Add UI controls to accelerate/decelerate simulation speed by multiplying the tick interval by 0.5x/2x (starting from 0.5s).
known_issues: Build/deployment attempts are failing (deployment didn't complete / AI couldn't process request).

existing_features.title: Create a fullscreen view that renders a 1000×1000 square grid with black grid lines and white cell backgrounds, where each cell has two visual states: live cells rendered black and dead cells rendered white.
Implement simulation initialization and reset behavior such that exactly 3000 live cells are randomly distributed within the central region of the 1000×1000 grid, with all other cells dead.

Add UI controls: Start (begin running the simulation), Pause (stop advancing generations while keeping the current state displayed), and Reset (generate a new random initial state of 3000 live cells in the central region).

Advance the simulation automatically every 0.5 seconds, producing a new generation by applying exactly these rules to each cell based on its 8 neighbors: (1) Birth: a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbors becomes live; (2) Survival: a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbors stays live; (3) Death: a live cell with 0 or 1 live neighbors dies (loneliness) and a live cell with more than 3 live neighbors dies (overpopulation). All other cases result in a dead cell.
Provide zoom in/out functionality for the grid view so the user can zoom into the cells and zoom back out while the simulation is running or paused.

Apply a coherent visual theme for the UI (controls + layout) that fits a minimalist, high-contrast technical simulation style using neutral tones (black/white/gray), consistent typography, and clear control hierarchy.
Change the rendered simulation grid from 1000×1000 to 200×200, keeping the fullscreen layout, black grid lines, white cell backgrounds, and the two cell states (live=black, dead=white).
Update the simulation initialization (first load / initial state) so that exactly 50 live cells are randomly distributed within the central region of the 200×200 grid, with all other cells dead.

Update the Reset behavior to generate a new random initial state with exactly 3000 live cells placed within the central region of the 200×200 grid (as requested), and reset the simulation to a paused/not-running state after reset.
Ensure the Start and Pause controls continue to work with the 200×200 grid: Start begins advancing generations automatically; Pause stops advancing while keeping the current grid state displayed.

Keep the simulation update interval at 0.5 seconds and apply the specified 8-neighbor rules each tick (birth on exactly 3 neighbors; survival on 2 or 3; death on 0–1 or >3). Ensure rules operate correctly at grid edges (define and implement a consistent edge policy).
Ensure the zoom in/out functionality continues to work correctly with the 200×200 grid while the simulation is running or paused.

Add two UI controls to adjust the simulation speed: a "Faster" control that halves the current generation tick interval on each press (e.g., 500ms → 250ms → 125ms …) and a "Slower" control that doubles the current tick interval on each press (e.g., 250ms → 500ms → 1000ms …).

Update the simulation loop so the tick interval is not a fixed constant and can be changed at runtime while the simulation is running or paused, without breaking Start/Pause/Reset behavior or the generation counter.
Display the current tick interval (or an equivalent speed indicator) in the controls panel in English so the user can see the active simulation speed.

new_feature_requests.summary: Fullscreen 200x200 raster animation with black grid lines and white background cells; live cells rendered black, dead cells white
Initialize with 50 randomly distributed live cells within the central region of the 200x200 grid
Reset regenerates a new random initial state of 3000 live cells within the central region
UI controls: Start to run the simulation, Pause to stop, Reset to regenerate initial state
